title: Expanding Datacenter Capacity with DVFS Boosting: A safe and scalable deployment experience
problem: Datacenters face unexpected demand surges requiring rapid capacity expansion. Traditional infrastructure growth is expensive and time-consuming, necessitating alternative techniques to boost computational capacity using existing hardware.
motivation: Efficient capacity expansion without proportional infrastructure costs enables datacenters to quickly respond to demand spikes while managing deployment complexity and operational safety.
method: DVFS (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling) boosting is deployed across datacenter processors to increase computational throughput by dynamically adjusting operating voltage and frequency. The approach includes safety mechanisms and validation procedures to ensure stable operation at scale across large distributed systems.
key_novelty: Practical, safe, and scalable deployment of DVFS boosting as a datacenter capacity expansion technique, demonstrated during high-demand periods.
contributions: Practical deployment methodology for DVFS boosting in production datacenters
Safe capacity expansion techniques without increasing physical infrastructure footprint
Scalable approach to handle unexpected demand using existing hardware capabilities
Deployment experience and lessons learned from large-scale DVFS rollout

metrics.other: capacity expansion ratio, deployment safety metrics

limitations: Specific performance metrics, energy trade-offs, and comparison with alternative expansion techniques not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: practical DVFS deployment for datacenter capacity
